ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy blues set with standout Smokestack Lightning and King Bee
ai_show_review.blurb: The show delivers a concise, high‑energy blues set anchored by Pigpen’s powerful harp on Smokestack Lightning and his gritty vocals on King Bee. Jerry’s early‑era guitar tone shines throughout, and the band locks in tight accompaniment. The soundboard tape captures the performance with good clarity despite minor processing artifacts.
ai_show_review.review: The February 12, 1967 Fillmore gig finds the Dead deep in their blues roots, launching straight into a scorching rendition of Smokestack Lightning that lets Pigpen’s harmonica howl over a driving rhythm section. Jerry’s sweet, early‑era guitar tone cuts through with crisp leads, even if a faint ring‑mod effect flickers on the tape. Without missing a beat, the band rolls into King Bee, where Pigpen’s gritty vocal growl and booming organ (though only hinted at in the mix) keep the momentum blazing. Phil holds down a solid low end while Bill and the rest of the rhythm crew keep everything tightly together, giving the set a cohesive, high‑octane feel that captures the raw excitement of the Summer of Love era. The soundboard source is surprisingly clear for its time, offering enough detail to hear each instrument’s character while preserving the live room energy.

best_recording.reason: Good‑quality soundboard tape that captures the high‑energy blues set with clear instrument separation, despite minor over‑processing artifacts.

key_highlights: Smokestack Lightning showcases Pigpen’s powerful harmonica and vocal grit
King Bee continues the blues momentum with tight band interplay
Jerry’s early‑era guitar tone shines throughout the set
Soundboard recording offers clear detail for a 1967 live performance
